routes.description: Move from an assumed fundamental reality to God-like perfection by treating unexplained nonmaximal parameters as arbitrary and extending arbitrariness reduction to greatness and other positive attributes.
routes.successCriteria: Establish that foundational limits require explanation, that fundamental reality possesses value or greatness, and that explained or eliminated limits support maximal or quasi-maximal perfection-relevant attributes.

motionBridge.description: Connect the removal of arbitrary foundational limits to maximal or quasi-maximal God-like attributes.

centralBridges.description: Supply reason to expect explanations for apparently arbitrary nonmaximal foundational parameters.
Establish that fundamental reality possesses value, greatness, or a value-entailing capacity.
Show that deeper necessitating grounds do not merely relocate the arbitrariness of limited outcomes.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify a comparative or defeasible role for the limits principle when it does not compel a unique worldview.
Restrict arbitrariness inheritance to grounding relations tight enough to transmit the relevant explanatory demand.

routes.description: Block the move from fundamental reality to God-like perfection by treating unexplained limits as one defeasible theoretical consideration and challenging the required explanatory, axiological, and maximality bridges.
routes.successCriteria: Show that rival theories may rationally retain foundational limits, that the foundation need not be minded or valuable, or that explained nonmaximal greatness remains compatible with imperfection.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the limits argument does not by itself determine a God-like or perfect foundation.

centralBridges.description: Require assessment of arbitrary limits within an all-things-considered comparison of rival theories.
Show that the support offered for explaining limits also supports rival principles unless a symmetry breaker is supplied.
Challenge the inference from valuable outcomes or enabling capacities to value or mentality in their foundation.
Preserve the possibility of an explained but nonmaximal degree of foundational greatness.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify the explanatory and modal senses in which a foundational parameter counts as arbitrary.
Test whether arbitrariness inheritance generalizes beyond necessitating grounding without unacceptable consequences.

sections.title: Scope and meaning of arbitrary limits
sections.rationale: This issue fixes what counts as an arbitrary foundational parameter and whether identifying such a parameter establishes a conclusion or instead contributes one consideration to comparative theory choice.

sections.title: Explanatory support and rival-principle parity
sections.rationale: The transition away from limited foundations depends on evidential support for explaining limits and on whether that support survives exceptions and structurally parallel causal principles.

sections.title: Foundation mentality and initial greatness
sections.rationale: Movement toward God-like perfection requires the foundation to possess some value or greatness, making mentality, productive ability, and axiological neutrality burden-relevant alternatives.

sections.title: Grounding value in fundamental reality
sections.rationale: The argument needs a bridge from derivative valuable states to value in their ultimate ground, while the opposing line distinguishes valuable properties from merely necessary enabling conditions.

sections.title: Explained limits and inherited arbitrariness
sections.rationale: The final transition to perfection turns on whether an essential or grounded nonmaximal limit can be nonarbitrary and whether necessitating grounds inherit the arbitrariness they purport to explain.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: A hypothesis about fundamental reality can be assessed through the unexplained arbitrariness of its intrinsic limits as well as through its capacity to produce observed effects.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: An arbitrary limit is an unexplained nonmaximal degree on a continuum where reason permits greater or lesser degrees, thereby inviting explanation of why that degree obtains.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Apparently irrelevant differences among possible fundamental limits, reinforced by the ordinary track record of further explanations, provide strong reason to think such limits require explanation.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: When the considerations supporting a principle equally support a competing principle, the original support is undercut unless a symmetry breaker distinguishes their applications.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: The greatness premise requires supplementary support from independent arguments for fundamental mentality or from the value of the foundation's power to produce value.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: Fundamental reality has intrinsic value because its foundational abilities make possible mind, matter, morality, and other valuable things.

chunk-003:c003-04.proposition: If a value-entailing property is grounded in something, its ground is also value-entailing, since positive aspects could not arise from a wholly value-free reality lacking valuable potential.

chunk-003:c003-06.proposition: A foundation's capacity to produce valuable states is itself valuable because without that capacity no value could arise anywhere in the resulting sequence.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: When a grounding property necessitates one arbitrary limited outcome rather than relevant alternatives, the ground inherits that arbitrariness and still calls for explanation.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Arbitrariness inheritance applies to strong necessitating grounding but not automatically to indeterministic creative explanation, so contingent creation need not transmit its arbitrariness to God.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The argument must distinguish being actually unexplained from being inexplicable and clarify whether arbitrariness involves genuine, apparent, or conceivable alternatives.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Because a non-theistic theory may entail fundamental limits and reject the limits premise, the argument alone cannot adjudicate between theories without comparing their broader virtues and costs.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: A track-record generalization toward further explanation is defeasible when a disputant has independent reason to expect that the fundamental case is an exception.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: The inductive, abductive, intuitive, and relevant-difference support used for the limits principle can also support rival causal principles whose consequences conflict with traditional theism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: A fundamental reality may be axiologically neutral because mindless foundations do not intuitively possess greatness, so establishing greatness appears to require first establishing mentality.

chunk-003:c003-02.proposition: The limits argument alone cannot establish theism because an additional premise or independent argument is required to show that the foundation is minded.

chunk-003:c003-03.proposition: The principle that value or greatness must be grounded in prior value or greatness lacks intuitive support and faces counterexamples and a conceivable falsifying model.

chunk-003:c003-07.proposition: Being a necessary condition for value does not make something valuable, just as necessary mathematical truths need not possess value merely because value could not exist without them.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: A foundation can have a nonmaximal but nonarbitrary degree of greatness when its limit is explained by metaphysical necessity or by the foundation's essential nature.

chunk-004:c004-06.proposition: The arbitrariness-inheritance principle risks equivocating between unexplainedness and comparative non-difference or implausibly making God inherit creation's arbitrary limits.
